item.title: Kyle Larson Keeps Finding a Way, and NASCAR’s Championship Is Now Within His Reach
item.description: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images MARTINSVILLE, Va. — Kyle Larson did not need to win Sunday’s Xfinity 500 to make a major statement in the NASCAR Cup Series championship battle. He simply needed to survive. The Hendrick Motorsports driver did exactly that, finishing ninth at Martinsville Speedway after a difficult afternoon for the No. 5 Chevrolet. The result was not particularly glamorous, but the championship implications were enormous. Larson leaves America’s Short Track with a 67-point advantage over Christopher Bell and a 70-point lead over Denny Hamlin. With the season finale approaching at Homestead-Miami Speedway, Larson is firmly in control of his pursuit of a third Cup Series championship. That is what separates championship-caliber drivers from everyone else. Even when the afternoon does not go according to plan, they find a way to protect the bigger objective. Larson Made the Most of a Difficult Martinsville Afternoon Martinsville is rarely an easy place to recover when a strategy call goes wrong. Larson experienced that firsthand Sunday. The No. 5 team elected to stay on track during an early pit strategy split. The decision ultimately hurt Larson’s track position, and he finished the opening stage in 23rd, one lap down. It was a frustrating position for a driver entering the weekend with an opportunity to clinch the championship. But Larson and his team never allowed the afternoon to become a disaster. A later caution helped him return to the lead lap. He steadily worked his way through the field and ultimately secured a ninth-place finish. Larson admitted afterward that there were opportunities missed during the race. He also acknowledged that the result could have been considerably worse. That assessment tells the story of his afternoon. He did not have the dominant car, but he avoided the kind of points disaster that could have reopened the championship fight. NASCAR’s official race coverage described the performance as a gritty, methodical effort. That is an appropriate description for a driver who understood exactly what was at stake. <Cite refs={[“turn261336search1″,”turn261336search0”]}/> The Championship Lead Is a Reflection of Larson’s Consistency Larson’s position entering the finale is not an accident. He has recorded three Cup victories in 2026, including a win at Talladega in October. His season also includes 15 top-five finishes and 20 top-10 results through 34 races. That combination has made him difficult to catch. There have been challenging weekends, but Larson has consistently demonstrated an ability to rebound. item.description: Mar 29, 2026; Martinsville, Virginia, USA. Photo Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Martinsville Speedway Remains NASCAR’s True Short-Track Treasure, From Grandfather Clocks to All-the-Way Hot Dogs MARTINSVILLE, Va. — NASCAR has changed dramatically since its earliest days. The cars are faster, the technology is more advanced and the sport’s schedule looks considerably different. But Martinsville Speedway still feels like Martinsville. The Virginia short track has been part of NASCAR’s premier series schedule every year since the division began in 1949. Its 0.526-mile paperclip layout remains one of the most distinctive challenges in stock car racing. Its famous grandfather clock remains one of the most recognizable trophies in the sport. And, of course, there are the hot dogs. Martinsville is not simply another stop on the NASCAR calendar. It is a reminder of the traditions that helped build the sport and the kind of experience that keeps generations of fans coming back. A Piece of NASCAR History That Refuses to Disappear H. Clay Earles opened Martinsville Speedway on Sept. 7, 1947, as a dirt track. NASCAR’s premier series arrived in 1949, when Red Byron won the first event. The track was paved in 1955, but its basic configuration remained intact. That decision helped preserve the character that makes Martinsville so different from larger facilities. At just over half a mile, there is little room for drivers to escape traffic. The long straightaways lead into tight, flat corners. Passing opportunities are limited, contact is common and patience can be just as important as speed. Martinsville demands a different kind of discipline. Drivers must manage their equipment, negotiate traffic and find opportunities without allowing frustration to take over. That combination has produced decades of memorable racing. It also explains why the track’s identity has survived as NASCAR has continued to evolve. The Grandfather Clock Means Something Different Winning at Martinsville comes with a trophy unlike anything else in NASCAR. The speedway introduced its grandfather clock trophy in 1964. The tradition began under Earles, who wanted race winners to receive something distinctive. The clocks were originally manufactured by Ridgeway Clocks, a company with local ties. The trophy became a signature part of Martinsville’s identity and remains one of the most coveted prizes in the sport. A grandfather clock is not an ordinary piece of racing hardware. It represents a victory at a track where history is part of the competition. For drivers, taking one home means joining a special group of Martinsville winners. For fans, it is another reminder that this place has traditions that cannot simply be replicated at a new facility. The Martinsville Hot Dog Is Part of the Experience Then there is the food. item.title: Dominik Szoboszlai provides injury update ahead of Fenerbahce vs Liverpool
item.description: Dominik Szoboszlai provides injury update ahead of Fenerbahce vs Liverpool Dominik Szoboszlai Injury Update as Liverpool Weigh Midfield Options for Fenerbahce Dominik Szoboszlai says he is fit again. Liverpool will hope he is right, because the timing matters. The midfielder returned in the 1-0 defeat to Arsenal at Anfield, his first appearance since 17 October after a hamstring problem suffered on international duty in September and October. It was a quiet comeback. Liverpool lost rhythm after he replaced Trey Nyoni, who had been one of the brighter performers. That happens. Players returning from muscle injuries rarely look sharp straight away. Before Sunday, Szoboszlai had only managed one outing since the break, starting against Brentford and lasting 30 minutes before coming off. So this has clearly been a stop-start period, even if the player now insists the issue is behind him. He said: “The worst thing is to be injured and watch the guys from the stands or on TV. I’m happy to be back, feeling good, feeling fit, and ready to go again on Wednesday. “Did I come back too soon? It stays secret. It’s very hard, you know. I’m the type of player, as you might know, that the last three seasons I want to play every 90 minutes but sometimes your body says ‘rest a little bit’ and my body told me to ‘stay calm, you’ve had enough games now’. “I missed games against (Manchester) City and LASK and then I felt again very good after a couple of days off but it seemed I wasn’t ready but sometimes it is my heart and I listen to my heart and not my body. “The plan to come in (from the bench). I was actually ready from the start but I’ve played 30 minutes and let’s see from now on.” Photo: IMAGO Midfield Competition Growing Fast There is another layer here. Szoboszlai is not walking back into a quiet midfield. He has already been used in several roles under Andoni Iraola this season, even filling in briefly at right-back, while Trey Nyoni’s progress has added real pressure. Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch are there too. Minutes have to be earned. Fenerbahce Start Now Looks Likely That said, Wednesday’s Champions League game against Fenerbahce looks like the obvious moment to push him back in. Rotation is expected, and Liverpool need points to strengthen their knockout hopes. If Szoboszlai is genuinely over the hamstring issue, this is the game to prove it. Fitness first, form second. Liverpool need both from him now.

item.title: “There’s No Bigger Insult From Him”: Insider Makes Thoughts Known on Bill Belichick’s Comments About Mario Cristobal’s Miami
item.description: Bill Belichick - UNC Tar Heels vs. TCU Horned Frogs © IMAGN Bill Belichick’s UNC suffered a tough 38-35 loss against the Miami Hurricanes on Saturday. The Tar Heels put up a strong fight, but a fourth-quarter fumble proved to be costly. After the game, Belichick seemed to take a dig at Hurricanes head coach Mario Cristobal’s defensive coordinator Corey Hetherman for running the same defensive schemes without any changes or creativity. This allowed the Tar Heels’ offense to score this many points against the No. 1 team in the nation. “They didn’t mix it up,” Belichick said. “They did what they did the whole game. They ran what they ran the whole game, which is honestly what they’ve been running the whole year. It wasn’t perfect on our part. We could have done a better job executing the play. The protection was good, but you know, we just end up holding the ball too long.” Having covered Belichick for years, insider Albert Breer well understood what the North Carolina head coach was trying to say regarding Hetherman. “I do know from covering Belichick for all those years—there’s no bigger insult from him to another staff than ‘they do what they do,'” Breer wrote on X. UNC led 28-24 with 11:46 remaining after Demon June scored on a one-yard touchdown run. Miami responded with a crucial drive, capped by Mark Fletcher Jr.’s two-yard touchdown run on fourth-and-one with 7:49 left to reclaim the lead. On UNC’s next possession, quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. was pressured by Miami defensive lineman Marquise Lightfoot, forcing a fumble. Defensive lineman Justin Scott recovered the ball at the UNC 37-yard line with 5:33 remaining. Miami then converted the turnover into a score as quarterback Darian Mensah connected with Malachi Toney for a nine-yard touchdown, extending Miami’s lead to 38-28 with just over two minutes remaining. Edwards connected with Trech Kekahuna for a touchdown with 1:38 remaining, cutting Miami’s lead to 38-35. In the end, Miami ran out the clock to hand UNC a heartbreaking loss. Bill Belichick Reacts After 103-Game Record Ends This was Bill Belichick’s first loss in his coaching career when his team had scored 35 or more points. He had previously been 103-0 in such games. “It’s the same every game,” Belichick said . “Look at the game. Things we did well, we try to keep doing well. Things we didn’t do well, we try to improve on. Get ready for a new game, a new opponent next week, which will be totally different than Miami. Every game’s different. None of them are the same. Each team has different players, different coordinators, different plays, different matchups. Each game’s its own entity, but you learn from the games you play, good and bad. So we do that every week, no matter what the outcome. It’s about the process.” The loss dropped UNC to 4-4 this season, while Miami extended its unbeaten run to eight games. item.title: Aston Villa skipper John McGinn admits it is 'not easy' playing under Unai Emery ahead of Champions League showdown at Camp Nou
item.description: Aston Villa Training Session and Press Conference - UEFA Super Cup 2026 - Getty Images Sport Aston Villa captain John McGinn has opened up on the intense tactical demands imposed by head coach Unai Emery as the Midlands club prepare to face Barcelona on Tuesday night. The Scotland international also praised the resilience of his side's new signings after bouncing back from a difficult start to the domestic season. Scottish midfielder praises summer recruits McGinn has hailed the mentality of Villa's younger summer additions after the club lost three of their first four Premier League fixtures, including a heavy 4-0 opening-day defeat away at Brighton and Hove Albion . That early slump followed a major transfer overhaul that saw established stars Emiliano Martinez, Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins leave Villa Park. Strong form across September and October has since revitalised their campaign. New arrivals embrace tactical system Having experienced slow starts during previous seasons under the Spanish tactician before going on sustained winning runs, the skipper was impressed by how quickly the fresh faces adapted to the manager's methods. Speaking to TNT Sports , McGinn said: "The players that have come in need to give themselves a lot of credit. It was a very difficult start. It's easier for us because we've been used to a poor start before, but they kept believing, kept trying to listen and take on board what the manager wants. "They allowed us to say, 'we'll be fine, don't worry, keep at it' and you're starting to see the best of Johan [Manzambi], and Alysson feels like a new player coming into this squad. It's not easy to play under this manager, but if you take the time to understand, be patient, and understand that in this system, it can bring out the best of you." Relentless standards drive European ambition Asked to expand on just how intense the former Sevilla and Villarreal boss can be on the training ground, the midfielder replied: "Quite, aye. It's what you want, he doesn't stop. Teams have had a small sniff of European football over the past few years, teams that have tried to compete with the big clubs. "He won't let us stop and get comfortable, he wants more, and that's why we're sitting in this stadium [Camp Nou] right now, because of how demanding he is. It's infectious, and it's our job to pass on that message in the dressing room. You either get on board with it or you don't." Perfect record tested in Catalonia Villa head into Tuesday's heavyweight clash in Spain sitting three points clear of Barcelona after winning all three of their opening Champions League fixtures. Only four other clubs - two-time reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain, Liverpool, Real Madrid and Real Betis - boast a 100 per cent record in the league phase so far. Securing a positive result at Camp Nou would further strengthen Villa's push for automatic knockout qualification.

item.title: Max Strus is back, but the Clippers' fourth-quarter problem isn't going anywhere
item.description: Los Angeles Clippers guard Kris Dunn (8) celebrates his tough and-one with his teammates during an NBA basketball game against the Toronto Raptors, Monday November 2nd, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. INGLEWOOD, Calif. – Max Strus finally got his first regular-season minutes in a Clippers uniform on Monday night, and for three quarters at Intuit Dome it looked like his return might be the thing that snapped this losing streak. Then the fourth quarter happened again, as the Toronto Raptors outscored the Clippers 47-27 in the final period to erase a 13-point deficit and walk out with a 125-118 win, handing Los Angeles its sixth straight loss after a season-opening win over Sacramento. How the Lead Slipped Away The Clippers controlled most of the night, holding Toronto to 22 points in the first quarter, going into halftime up 63-52 and building their lead to as many as 16 before taking a 91-78 cushion into the fourth. Toronto came out of the break by slowing everything down and attacking the rim, and the Clippers fouled their way right back into trouble, with the Raptors going 31-of-48 from the free-throw line on a night when Los Angeles was whistled for 34 fouls and had both Brook Lopez and Kris Dunn foul out. The Clippers still had a 109-103 lead late, but Toronto answered with another run, and Scottie Barnes hit a turnaround jumper with 2:08 left that put the Raptors in front for good. Barnes finished with 22 points, 15 rebounds and eight assists, with 15 of those points coming in the fourth quarter, while Immanuel Quickley scored 27 and RJ Barrett added 26. "We fouled too much," Strus said after the game. "They slowed the game down. They got free throws. They stopped the clock a lot and that gave up our lead." Strus had 11 points in 23 minutes in his first game since suffering a partial plantar fascia tear in his right foot during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Golden State in Hawaii. Ty Lue, who coached through an illness that kept him out of his pregame press conference, pointed to Toronto's size after the game, especially once Lopez fouled out. "I thought the size really bothered us around the rim," Lue said. item.title: ‘On another day…’ – Ex-PGMOL chief says Liverpool were ‘fortunate’ with one decision on Sunday
item.description: ‘On another day…’ – Ex-PGMOL chief says Liverpool were ‘fortunate’ with one decision on Sunday A former Premier League referee believes that Liverpool were ‘fortunate’ with one incident in particular from their defeat to Arsenal on Sunday. The Reds were left incensed by the failure of referee Andy Madley and VAR Stuart Attwell to spot a clear shirt tug by Jurrien Timber on Alexander Isak inside the penalty area, a decision that Steven Gerrard lamented as ‘ an absolute embarrassment ‘. It has even prompted debate as to whether the Swedish striker – who stayed on his feet and didn’t protest – could’ve done more to influence the officials, but earlier in the match there was an incident which had the Gunners complaining. Inside the opening minute, Trey Nyoni caught Martin Odegaard on the Achilles but avoided a yellow card, just as he did for a foul on Kai Havertz shortly afterwards. Hackett: Nyoni and Liverpool were ‘fortunate’ Former PGMOL chief executive Keith Hackett feels that the Liverpool midfielder was quite lucky not to have been at least booked over those two early fouls, especially the first one. He told Football Insider : “First of all, it doesn’t matter whether it’s the first or the 90th minute; the laws of the game apply. For me, if you like, the least amount of punishment on that is a yellow card. I think that challenge is reckless. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) “On another day… and because it is early, I think that’s why he’s fortunate not to get a red. He’s raked his studs down the Achilles of his opponent. “However you look at that, that has to receive a sanction; so for me, I’ll give him slight benefit of the doubt, slight mistiming, whatever you want, but he has to come out of that with a yellow card at the very minimum.” Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Liverpool got away with one in that instance Taking the challenge on Odegaard in isolation, Nyoni probably should’ve been booked for the nature of the foul, irrespective of it being in the first minute. We acknowledge that the Liverpool youngster got away with one there. Would he have flown into the tackle on Havertz had he already been on a yellow card? Maybe not, but to us it’s one of those where a word of warning from Madley would’ve sufficed. In that scenario, we suspect that Andoni Iraola may have substituted the 19-year-old much earlier than the 59th minute, for fear that the midfielder was a red card in waiting and was showing a bit too much enthusiasm on his first Premier League start. Nyoni and Liverpool were lucky in that instance, but don’t let this be a case of two wrongs making a right when weighing it up against the penalty we should’ve had for Timber’s shirt tug on Isak. Football stakeholders are right to demand higher standards of officiating at top-flight level, and the onus is on Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb to ensure that his referees do better.

item.title: Anthony Gordon targets football’s “Top Bracket” after Barcelona move, inspired by Harry Kane’s rise
item.description: Anthony Gordon targets football’s “Top Bracket” after Barcelona move, inspired by Harry Kane’s rise Anthony Gordon hopes his summer move to Barcelona can put him in the 'top bracket' of footballers. Gordon signed for the Spanish champions from Newcastle United in the summer and has had an impressive start in LaLiga. The 25-year-old has two goals and four assists in nine league appearances and has formed part of a freescoring attack under Hansi Flick. Gordon believes his move to Barcelona can see him enter the conversation around the best wingers in the game. He pointed to the example of Harry Kane, who was last month named winner of the Ballon d'Or. Gordon believes Kane's move to Bayern Munich has helped his profile, with the England captain now competing regularly on the biggest stage for major trophies. The England international said competing for the biggest trophies was the driving factor behind his summer switch to Spain, and believes accolades will arrive if he performs for Barcelona on a consistent basis. Anthony Gordon eyes major trophies and a place among the game’s best at Barcelona "It's the same with H [Harry Kane]. He was at Spurs for a long time and he had an unbelievable Premier League career. But because Spurs didn't win any trophies, it maybe didn't put him in that top, top bracket that he's in now," Gordon said to TNT Sports. "I think his move to Bayern Munich has put him on another level because he's been able to add trophies. He gets to show his ability on the highest, highest stages, in the later rounds of the Champions League . "That's what these clubs do and that's why I've always dreamt of playing for this club, because everybody watches Barcelona. We get to fight on every front for the biggest trophies. When you perform in the biggest games, that's when the accolades and everything you want comes true."

item.title: 🚨 BREAKING: Nuno Espirito Santo sacked by West Ham
item.description: 🚨 BREAKING: Nuno Espirito Santo sacked by West Ham West Ham have parted company with head coach Nuno Espírito Santo following their disappointing start to the season. The Portuguese coach has come under increasing pressure following a poor start to the Championship campaign, with West Ham sitting eighth in the table after 13 matches. A 3-1 home defeat to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday, their second consecutive loss at the London Stadium, intensified scrutiny of Nuno. And now it's been confirmed that the former Spurs and Wolves boss has been shown the door in east London. A statement read: "West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect. "Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track. "Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed. "West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future. "The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway. "Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of squad preparations ahead of tomorrow evening’s EFL Championship fixture at Cardiff City, and the Club will make no further comment until the appointment of the new Head Coach is confirmed."

item.title: Analysis: No. 25 BYU makes early claim to be an elite offensive unit in opening win over Ohio State
item.description: BYU Cougars forward Jaxon Kohler (0) drives to the hoop for a layup during a game against Ohio State at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News At one point this offseason, Kevin Young claimed his new-look Cougars would be the “most prolific shooting team” he’d had thus far at BYU. Early on in Monday’s season opener against Ohio State, however, Young’s squad looked like anything but. The first 10 minutes of the regular season saw BYU miss 10 of 13 field goal attempts, with seven misses coming from behind the arc. But when the shots started falling for the Cougars, they seemingly never stopped. Following the initial slump, No. 25-ranked BYU shot 64% from the field and 63% from 3-point range — averaging 1.4 points per possession in all — to bury the visiting Ohio State Buckeyes 94-83 at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City. Ohio State hadn’t dropped a regular season opener since 2003, but surrendering 60 second half points to Young’s Cougars now puts the Buckeyes in unfamiliar territory: an 0-1 record. “I think we just played to our identity,” Young told reporters postgame. “I thought in the first half they put us in mud a little bit, particularly the first five or six minutes. But the message for our guys coming into the game was just don’t make stuff up. This can be a very dynamic offensive team, so to hang 60 points in a half on somebody of that caliber is impressive.” All five BYU starters scored in double figures, a feat the Cougars hadn’t achieved since their last Delta Center appearance against Cal Baptist in December of 2025. And considering those BYU players were all competing in their first regular season contest together on Monday, scoring 94 total points against a veteran-heavy, reigning NCAA tournament team from the Big Ten should feel all the more encouraging — especially when 83 of those points were scored in the game’s final 30 minutes. “It’s funny that we scored that many (points) because it kind of felt like (the offense) was stuck in the first half,” said BYU guard Collin Chandler, who made his Cougars debut Monday just 20 minutes south of his hometown of Farmington. “We felt like we couldn’t get anything to flow. It’s a really good sign for us that we can turn around like that by just talking about it and wearing teams down. I feel like that’s what happened tonight.” Rob Wright III, BYU’s lone returning starter, led the offensive charge with 33 points, five assists and just one turnover, marking one of his best outings as a Cougar and validating his preseason buzz as an All-America and Big 12 Player of the Year candidate. item.title: Stats: Barcelona boast impressive home record against English clubs ahead of Aston Villa clash
item.description: Stats: Barcelona boast impressive home record against English clubs ahead of Aston Villa clash Barcelona will look to extend their impressive home record against English opposition when they welcome Aston Villa to the Spotify Camp Nou in the UEFA Champions League. Hansi Flick’s side needs a victory to strengthen their position in the league phase standings after suffering a defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing. The visitors arrive with a contrasting record across competitions. Although Aston Villa have experienced inconsistent results in the Premier League, they have made an excellent start to their Champions League campaign, collecting nine points from their opening three matches. However, the Catalans can draw confidence from a remarkable historical record against English clubs on home soil. Barcelona have lost just twice at home against English opposition Barcelona face Aston Villa next. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images) Statistically, across 38 European fixtures against English teams, Barcelona have recorded 23 victories, 13 draws and just two defeats . That means they have lost only 5.2% of their home matches against representatives of English football. The record becomes even more impressive when looking exclusively at Champions League encounters. At the Camp Nou, Barcelona have registered 13 wins, six draws and only one defeat against English opposition in the competition. Liverpool the only English club to beat Barcelona at home Barcelona’s only home defeat against an English opponent in the Champions League came against Liverpool during the 2006-07 campaign. Barcelona have a great home record against an English side in the Champions League. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) The Reds secured a 2-1 victory in the first leg of their round-of-16 tie, handing the Catalans a rare European setback on their own ground. Since that encounter, Barcelona have avoided defeat in 15 consecutive home European matches against English clubs, recording ten victories and five draws. Maintaining that sequence for almost two decades is a testament to the consistency of Barcelona’s performances against Premier League opposition. Unai Emery’s side will arrive in Catalonia with confidence from their perfect start in the Champions League, having collected all nine available points. Their domestic inconsistency, however, makes their European performances particularly interesting and Barcelona can ride on that to hand them their first European defeat of the season.

item.title: Former Real Madrid star accuses Mourinho of repeated tactical mistakes: ‘Should have dropped Vinicius from the beginning’
item.description: Former Real Madrid star accuses Mourinho of repeated tactical mistakes: ‘Should have dropped Vinicius from the beginning’ Real Madrid have enjoyed a resurgence in recent weeks following some tactical tweaks from Jose Mourinho. It all started with the remarkable comeback in Rome, where Los Blancos came back from 3-1 down to win 4-3 in the final 10 minutes of the game. The Portuguese tactician made important changes to his line-up from that point onwards, moving Federico Valverde to right-back and bringing Bernardo Silva into midfield. However, not everyone is convinced by the Portuguese manager’s decisions. Former Los Blancos striker Poli Rincon has revealed that he remains unconvinced. Rincon questions Mourinho’s handling of Bernardo Silva During an appearance on Ruben Martin’s YouTube channel, Rincon argued that Mourinho took too long to identify the tactical shortcomings. “Jose Mourinho didn’t want to play Bernardo Silva in central midfield, and he ended up using that lineup in El Clasico because he had no other choice,” Rincon claimed (h/t Defensa Central ). Bernardo Silva has proved to be a transformative inclusion in Real Madrid’s midfield. (Picture credit: Real Madrid website) “The best thing the coach has done is correct his mistakes, because he got things wrong in the opening matches of the season.” The former Madrid striker was highly critical of the partnership between Federico Valverde and Aurelien Tchouameni. “The manager made many mistakes from the beginning of the season until he realised the reality: Vinicius cannot be a starter, and Fede Valverde and Tchouameni cannot play together in the double pivot,” he explained. Rincon demands more attacking football from Real Madrid Rincon believes Mourinho should set his team up to be more attacking and should have trusted Madrid’s technically gifted players earlier. “Jose Mourinho has players capable of playing football, not just defending and sitting deep. He should have dropped Vinicius and played Diomande from the beginning. And if he also plays Carlos Espi, even better, ” he added. His criticism comes after Mourinho won his last six games with Real Madrid, including a 2-1 away win at the Spotify Camp Nou . Mourinho deserves massive credit for his tactical adaptations. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) While it is true that the team have looked much better since Bernardo Silva came into midfield , it is not true that Mourinho took too long to recognise this. It is still very early in the season, and the Portuguese manager has made the changes before the most important part of the campaign begins. If anything, Mourinho deserves credit for accepting that something was not working and adapting his tactics accordingly. Rincon may not be Mourinho’s biggest fan, but Madrid’s resurgence is completely down to his methods, and the important thing is that the results have started to come.

item.title: NZ's Ponga back in World Cup contention after broken arm
item.description: Kalyn Ponga trained this week with a black bandage around his recently broken left arm [Getty Images] New Zealand have named Kalyn Ponga on the reserve list for their Rugby League World Cup semi-final against Tonga - just three weeks after he broke his forearm. And hooker Phoenix Crossland has also been included on the reserve list after completing a four-match ban imposed for the tackle that ruled Nathan Cleary out of the World Cup. Ponga suffered a broken arm on 15 October during the opening game of the tournament, which New Zealand lost to Australia in a thrilling encounter. The full-back played on for around 20 minutes with the injury as Australia narrowly triumphed 24-22, before having to go for surgery . But even at the time, head coach Stacey Jones expressed hope that Ponga would be fit for the final on 15 November if New Zealand got there. Crossland, meanwhile, is back available after missing the entire group stage as he served his suspension. item.title: David Moyes gives icy response to Jack Grealish questions as Everton disciplinary exile continues
item.description: Everton v Manchester United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Jack Grealish’s attempt to reignite his career at Everton has hit a significant stumbling block after the playmaker was excluded from the matchday squad for the second time in a single week. Toffees boss David Moyes has remained cagey regarding the specific reasons for the England international's absence, heightening speculation around the player's long-term future at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Grealish frozen out by Toffees Everton secured a Monday night victory over Newcastle, but Grealish was entirely absent from the matchday squad. It marked his second consecutive omission, having already missed last week's Carabao Cup triumph against the same opponent. The 31-year-old was initially sidelined for a reported "breach of club discipline", a stance Moyes publicly supported at the time. While the club officially attributed this latest absence to a lack of fitness, the continued exile highlights the player's precarious standing on Merseyside. Moyes refuses to elaborate on absence Speaking to the BBC , Moyes remained tight-lipped regarding the ongoing situation. The veteran manager offered little clarity on when the midfielder might feature again for the Toffees. "He's unavailable at the moment and we will make a decision with the club when we think that availability comes back," Moyes stated. When pushed on whether the absence was genuinely fitness-related, as the club had claimed, the manager offered a blunt reply: "All I'm giving out is that he is unavailable at the moment." Attempting to probe the alleged disciplinary breach yielded a similarly defensive response, with Moyes simply adding: "I can't comment on that." A promising loan spell turns sour Grealish returned to Hill Dickinson Stadium hoping to revive a stuttering career. The £100 million man is in the final months of his Manchester City contract and desperately needs consistent minutes after gradually falling down the pecking order under Pep Guardiola following their 2023 treble win. His previous Everton loan yielded two goals in 22 appearances before being derailed by injury. Despite earning a return to the club based on those earlier performances, the playmaker has managed just six outings this term before seemingly falling out of favour entirely. Coventry clash looms for Everton Everton host Coventry on Friday night, though it remains highly uncertain if Grealish will be reinstated to the squad. While Moyes insists a pathway back to the first team still exists, the midfielder faces an uphill battle to regain the manager's trust and salvage his rapidly fading season.

item.title: Harry Kane would swap Ballon d’Or glory for Champions League triumph with Bayern Munich
item.description: Harry Kane would swap Ballon d’Or glory for Champions League triumph with Bayern Munich Harry Kane has said he would swap his Ballon d'Or success to win the Champions League with Bayern Munich this season. Kane was named winner of the Ballon d'Or last month, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to football's biggest individual honour. The 33-year-old was recognised after scoring 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern last season, a return that helped the German giants to a domestic treble. Bayern lost to eventual winners Paris Saint-Germain in last season's Champions League semi-finals and Kane is keen to secure elusive European success this season. Speaking ahead of Bayern Munich's meeting with Atletico Madrid in the league phase tonight, Kane said he would swap individual accolades for team success. "Team trophies are why we play football," he said at a pre-match press conference. "The team aspect of our sport is really, really important. The Ballon d'Or last week was one of the best feelings I've had in my life and my career. But to have moments with the team, celebrations with the club - to be able to life the Champions League with Bayern would be an incredible feeling. "I would choose the Champions League, but I have the opportunity to do both. Let's see what happens." Bayern are currently 14th in the league phase table , having drawn their last two Champions League fixtures. The German champions beat Bodo/Glimt in their opener but have since dropped points against Viking and Arsenal. Kane is the joint-leading scorer in this season's Champions League with four goals in three games. He leads the standings alongside five other forwards, including Manchester City striker Erling Haaland and Borussia Dortmund's Serhou Guirassy.

item.title: How 'student of coaching' Contepomi took unexpected path
item.description: Felipe Contepomi took over from Michael Cheika as Argentina head coach in 2023 [Getty Images] Back when Michael Cheika was Felipe Contepomi's head coach at Leinster two decades ago, did the former Argentina boss believe his immediate successor with the Pumas would go on to have such a successful post-playing career? "No, I didn't," he says without missing a beat. The pair overlapped for four seasons in Dublin, building towards the province's first Heineken Cup in 2009 before the fly-half departed for Toulon that summer having missed the final through injury. At a time when he was keeping a young Johnny Sexton out of the 10 jersey, Contepomi was a talisman during what was a foundational spell in the club's history. Conversely, it was such abundant talent that made Cheika doubt his then fly-half's future lay in coaching. "He was obviously a highly-skilled player and you know what they say about some of the best players? They don't make the greatest coaches because they think everyone can do what they could do and they actually can't." Thirteen years after their paths diverged, and after Contepomi had spent four seasons as Leinster's attack coach, Cheika was bringing his former player into the Pumas set-up as his assistant. What changed in the intervening years? "Felipe is different, right?" says Cheika of the man who brings his Argentina team to face Ireland in Dublin on Friday night. "He's come into coaching raw and has had to take a step back, go and self-reflect on how much he really wants to do that. He went to Leinster and learnt his craft properly there with some good coaches around him in a team and an environment that he felt absolutely comfortable in. "He understood what he had to do to become a quality coach first up and then a head coach, which is different to just being a coach as well." Cheika's successor as Leinster, Joe Schmidt, spent three seasons at the province between Contempomi's stints as a player and an assistant, but considers the former playmaker a "pretty good friend" from their time spent in opposing coaching boxes. The pair went head-to-head in the Rugby Championships of 2024 and 2025 while Schmidt was in charge of Australia. Each won two of those four contests, although the most comprehensive victory was Argentina's 67–27 triumph in 2024. The pair would often meet for a drink or coffee before those Tests with Schmidt echoing Cheika's assertion that Contempomi possesses an ability to use his past playing ability as a complement in his coaching. "I'd have a really high opinion of Felipe as a master of playing the game, but as a student of coaching the game," said the former Ireland head coach. "I think he blends the two to be a really good coach." It should perhaps come as no surprise that Contempomi has shown such aptitude for study as a coach having split his time in Dublin between playing and working to become medical doctor. item.description: Jesus de Miguel, playing for former side Castellon, in 2024 [Getty Images] Tenerife say Jesus de Miguel's medical condition has "worsened" after the striker sustained a serious injury during a Spanish second division match. The 30-year-old suffered head and chest injuries during Monday's home game against Andorra, after a heavy collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off for his challenge. Spanish media, including Marca , reported De Miguel had a cardiac arrest in an ambulance and was resuscitated by paramedics on the way to hospital. An initial statement from Tenerife on Monday said De Miguel was "stable" in hospital, despite the "severity of his condition". However, a further update from the club in the early hours of Tuesday morning said the striker's "medical condition has worsened neurologically" and there would be "more information in the coming hours". Tenerife and Andorra were drawing 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred. Owono had run towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel. De Miguel lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital. Players from both teams were visibly distressed by the incident, with a number of De Miguel's team-mates in tears. The referee showed Owono a straight red card before abandoning the match. A statement from Andorra said: "We want to send all our strength and best wishes to Jesus de Miguel after the serious incident suffered during today's match. "We hope he recovers soon. While the Spanish tactician is highly admired by the Red Devils' hierarchy, his sweeping authority in the West Midlands makes any prospective switch difficult to pull off. Red Devils admire Spanish tactician According to TEAMtalk , United view the former Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain boss as a standout candidate should they part company with Carrick. Despite publicly backing their former midfielder , Old Trafford officials are quietly drawing up a shortlist of replacements behind the scenes. Complete control underpins Midlands success Over several years in Birmingham, the Spaniard has established immense authority across the club's football operations, transforming Villa into regular top-four challengers and Europa League winners. That autonomy has been central to his success, as the hierarchy in the West Midlands have given his methods and decision-making full backing. The report notes that another shot at an elite European giant would be tough for Emery to turn down, especially as his previous stints with PSG and Arsenal ended without the silverware or satisfaction he wanted. However, stepping into the dugout at Old Trafford would mean operating within a very different executive structure. Because he would not be granted the same sweeping power he currently enjoys at Villa, that reduced influence is seen as a major stumbling block to any deal. Boardroom split over leading contenders Alongside the question of whether Emery would accept less control in Manchester, internal discussions at Old Trafford have also highlighted two other frontrunners for the post. item.title: ‘I want a full investigation’ – Seahawks fans are demanding NFL action after loss to the Bears
item.description: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images Seattle Seahawks fans have been left outraged by a decision going against their team during Monday night’s defeat to the Chicago Bears. Mike Macdonald’s team have been provided with a real wake up call on the back of their emphatic victory against the Kansas City Chiefs. The Seahawks simply do not look like a team capable of going back-to-back after their Super Bowl win earlier in the season. It was another jittery performance for Sam Darnold in the pocket as his fourth quarter interception sealed the defeat for the Seahawks. However, there was a moment earlier in the game involving Darnold that left fans furious. No call from the referees on what seemed like an incredibly late hit on Darnold – who had given himself up by sliding – left Seahawks fans stunned by the lack of protection provided to their quarterback by the officials. Seattle Seahawks demand NFL ‘investigation’ after no call on Sam Darnold There is no getting around just how poorly Darnold has played this season after returning from his injury. Turnovers have been a major issue for Seattle and Darnold has thrown at least one touchdown in every game he has completed this season. However, fans clearly want to see their quarterback given a lot more protection by the referees than what was on display on Monday night. ‘I want a full investigation,’ one fan replied to the footage of Darnold being clattered by linebacker Devin Bush. ‘I don’t see how that hit wasn’t penalised. item.description: Barcelona rout Alavés 6-1 to retake LaLiga lead before top-two clash with Atlético Barcelona beat Alavés 6-1 at Spotify Camp Nou to go back to the top of LaLiga. Within hours, Barcelona took the place back. Hansi Flick’s side dismantled Alavés in front of their own fans. The result ended a two-game losing run after defeats to PSG and Real Madrid. item.title: FIFA to share documents related to World Cup sell-off plan
item.description: FIFA will release details of President Gianni Infantino’s aborted plan to sell off stakes in future World Cups to private investors, but they will not be shared with the public. Reports in the British media said members of the FIFA Council, the main decision-making body of football’s world governing body, will be given access to “key documents” related to the proposal, named FIFA Forward Enterprise. However, they can only view them under “strict protocols to preserve confidentiality”, the reports said. Those include the 37 members of the council having to register for an in-person appointment to view selected paperwork in Zurich, Switzerland, in the next two weeks. Infantino attends the opening game of the 2026 U-20 Women’s World Cup opening match in Katowice, Poland [File: Beata Zawrzel/AP Photo] The news came out late on Monday, the deadline European football’s governing body, UEFA, had set for FIFA to release details about the $4.2bn scheme and answer questions about how the proposal came about and who approved it before the plans were dropped in July amid a worldwide backlash. UEFA set the deadline after a tense council meeting at which Infantino apologised for the proposal but provided no details about how the plan was formed. He asked council members to submit their questions in writing. UEFA is leading attempts to remove Infantino before or at the FIFA presidential election on March 18 in Rabat, Morocco. Infantino, who was elected in 2016, is seeking a fourth term through 2031.

Imagine explaining to Houston that its next big football storyline isn’t a playoff run, a quarterback controversy or another coaching change. It’s finding out which state gets to call the Texans its own. In this political playbook, James Talarico has a bold new strategy for Texas football: send the Texans packing. Maybe Nashville needs another football team. Perhaps Oklahoma City wants to take a swing at the NFL. Wherever the imaginary destination might be, Houston fans would have one question: Why should their team leave Texas? Still, the joke writes itself when Texas politics and professional football collide. Houston is one of the state’s biggest sports markets. The Texans represent a major part of its identity, and fans have spent years waiting for the franchise to deliver a deep playoff run. The last thing those supporters want is another reason to worry about their team’s future. Talarico has plenty of real policy positions to defend, particularly on economic regulation and the role of government. Texas voters can debate those positions without pretending he has called for an NFL relocation. For Texans fans, the ideal political game plan is simple: Keep the team in Houston, keep the football in Texas and leave the relocation rumors to the sports satire column.

item.title: ‘Have You Seen Him Play Football?’ ‘Mind Your Business’ — Dan Orlovsky Wins No Fans in Urging Lamar Jackson-Less Ravens To Go After Former Gators Star
item.description: ‘Have You Seen Him Play Football?’ ‘Mind Your Business’ — Dan Orlovsky Wins No Fans in Urging Lamar Jackson-Less Ravens To Go After Former Gators Star The Baltimore Ravens aren’t ready to give up on their season just yet. After missing the playoffs last year, they made a major change at head coach, bringing in Jesse Minter to replace John Harbaugh. However, injuries to Lamar Jackson have derailed their plans once again. That has led to speculation about whether the Ravens could make a trade to address their quarterback situation. Several names have come up as potential targets, but one suggestion from Dan Orlovsky was met with a resounding no from much of the fan base. Dan Orlovsky’s Suggestion for Lamar Jackson Replacement Doesn’t Sit Well With Ravens Fans Jackson was playing at a high level when healthy and helped the Ravens get off to a 3-1 start. But without him, the team dropped to 4-3. Jackson returned in Week 8, only for his comeback to last just one offensive snap. The Ravens have since fallen to 4-4, with a brutal stretch of the schedule still ahead. However, the team isn’t ready to throw in the towel. As potential replacements at quarterback continue to come up, Orlovsky added another name to the conversation. “If you’re the Ravens, why would you not call Indy about Anthony Richardson?” the ESPN analyst tweeted. The Indianapolis Colts selected Richardson fourth overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. One of the biggest concerns surrounding him coming out of Florida was his limited experience as a starter. After two inconsistent, injury-plagued seasons, Richardson lost the starting job to Daniel Jones in 2025 and later requested a trade. item.title: Texas Could Land Another NHL Team, But James Talarico’s Economic Agenda May Make the League Pivot
item.description: Sep 22, 2026; Calgary, Alberta, CAN; Calgary Flames center Morgan Frost (16) controls the puck against the Vancouver Canucks during the second period at Scotiabank Saddledome. Mandatory Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images HOUSTON, Texas — Texas is closer than ever to potentially landing another NHL franchise. But the state’s political direction could become an important part of the conversation surrounding major sports investments. The NHL is evaluating Houston and Austin as potential destinations for its 33rd franchise. The project could involve approximately $3.5 billion in combined expansion and arena investment. That is an enormous opportunity for Texas. A new NHL franchise would bring jobs, tourism, corporate partnerships and another major professional sports destination to the state. But prospective owners need confidence in the economic environment surrounding their investments. James Talarico has called for tighter federal regulations on data centers, including additional infrastructure requirements and greater local authority over development decisions. His proposals do not directly target NHL arenas. However, they raise questions about how his broader approach to regulation would affect major private investments. Texas has built a reputation as a destination for businesses and major sporting developments. A new hockey franchise would strengthen that reputation. Talarico should explain how he would encourage major private investment while pursuing additional federal oversight of industries that depend on substantial infrastructure. Texas has an opportunity to become an even bigger sports destination. It should not take that opportunity for granted.

item.title: Do Ferrari need rules of engagement? F1 Q&A
item.description: The first-lap battle between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Mexico allowed Red Bull's Max Verstappen to get through and take second place, before going on to win the race [Reuters] Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1's youngest world champion by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finishing second. Hamilton was unhappy with his team-mate Charles Leclerc and said Ferrari "have to have some serious talks behind closed doors" after fighting between their two drivers cost them victory in Mexico. BBC F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions. McLaren has its 'papaya' rules, is it now time for Ferrari to introduce its 'Maranello' rules? - John The battle between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc on the opening lap in Mexico, and the fall-out from it, provided a perfect illustration of the problems that can arise when a team has two top drivers of equal status. Hamilton's point after the race was that Ferrari would have won the race - probably got a one-two - if the pair had worked together on that first lap. "When your team-mate works against you and then you lose positions like that, it's definitely tough," he said. Team boss Frederic Vasseur aldo bemoaned the loss of a potential one-two, admitting he was "frustrated". Leclerc argued that it takes two to tango. "I could be also unhappy with how much he pushed me off track out of Turn One," he said, "but it is racing. When you are fighting for a win it is the way it should be." Leclerc added: "At the end we both did a mistake going into Turn Four. It's not like we had contact whatsoever. We both went straight and that gave the opportunity for Max to overtake. So I don't think it should be that much of a talking point." Clearly there is a problem here. It's not the first time the Ferrari drivers' competing priorities have caused issues this year, and Vasseur has yet to find a way to manage it effectively, and get the drivers to buy into what he decides. In this case, the two drivers are expressing two completely different, but valid, points of view. Hamilton is thinking of the team result - which conveniently also meant a win for him - Leclerc primarily about the fact that they are allowed to race for the win. The problem is that the team's result was compromised and a win thrown away. Had Verstappen not passed Hamilton as a consequence of the incident, Leclerc could have given the place back by Turn 11 as was required by the rules. But once Verstappen was between them, continuing in the lead was Leclerc's only realistic option. This is a really difficult situation for Vasseur to handle. The team wants to win the race as first priority, but the same applies to each individual driver. Sometimes those two competing priorities clash. And if Ferrari ever get themselves a car that can compete for the title, it will only get harder, because the stakes for both drivers are then much higher. McLaren
